etymologies.etymologyHTML: From the Old French verb retaillier.

definitions.definition: (business) The sale of goods directly to the consumer, encompassing the storefronts, mail-order, websites, etc., and the corporate mechanisms, branding, advertising, etc. that support them.
(colloquial) Retail price; full price; an abbreviated expression, meaning the full suggested price of a particular good or service, before any sale, discount, or other deal.
Of or relating to the (actual or figurative) sale of goods or services directly to individuals.

quote.citation: 1997 December 28, “Freddie Mac establishes existing-home sales division”, in Deseret News:
quote.text: "This is a very retail approach for us," Czerw said. "But when you buy one out of every six home loans in the US, you are going to have a constant flow ..."

quote.citation: 1999 December 12, Naedine Joy Hazell, “TRAVEL INSIDER; Airport Malls Redefine 'Shopping on the Fly'”, in Los Angeles Times:
quote.text: The future for Bradley International Airport near Hartford, Conn., also looks very retail. Plans call for $156 million to expand the main terminal,

quote.citation: 2010 September 17, “Sarah Palin's visit to Iowa keeps fans guessing”, in Des Moines Register:
quote.text: But even with her level of celebrity, it would be very hard to win a race without engaging voters in a very retail way.

quote.citation: 2024 January 19, Jonathan Freedland, “There is still a way to stop Donald Trump – but time is running out”, in The Guardian‎[1], →ISSN:
quote.text: When the New York Post branded Ron DeSantis “DeFuture” in 2022 […] , it had not reckoned on the Florida governor being astonishingly awkward with the basics of retail politics: smiling, shaking hands, interacting with other people.

definitions.definition: Direct to consumers, in retail quantities, or at retail prices.
To sell at retail, or in small quantities directly to customers.

quote.citation: 2005, Plato, translated by Lesley Brown, Sophist, page 223d:
quote.text: a half part of this purveying is carried on within the city and is called retailing.

definitions.definition: (archaic) To sell secondhand, or in broken parts.
To repeat or circulate (news or rumours) to others.

quote.citation: 1934, Agatha Christie, chapter 12, in Murder on the Orient Express, London: HarperCollins, published 2017, page 157:
quote.text: He retailed to them the curious interchange of phrases he had overheard on the journey from Aleppo.

quote.citation: 1982, Lawrence Durrell, Constance (Avignon Quintet), Faber & Faber, published 2004, page 762:
quote.text: He became quite pale as he retailed these stories to Constance.

quote.citation: 1998 February 1, Alan Ryan, “Hot Spots (review of The Warrior's Honor: Ethnic War and the Modern Conscience by Michael Ignatieff)”, in The New York Times‎[2]:
quote.text: The fantasies of blood libel that Bosnian Serbs retailed about Bosnian Muslims were the fantasies that Rhinelanders had centuries earlier retailed about the Jews they had murdered.
